why: Each (key, field) keeps an append-only list of versions [start, end, value]. A SET closes the open version and appends a new one, and a DELETE closes it. GET_WHEN(at) is a binary search for the last version whose start is <= at, followed by a check that at < end. That combines the week's two themes, design and binary search.
hints: Never overwrite history. Think of each field as a timeline of half-open intervals [start, end).
A version ends at the earliest of start+ttl (when ttl > 0), the next SET, or the next DELETE. On a SET or DELETE at time t, set the open version's end to min(end, t).

Store, per (key, field), parallel lists of starts, ends and values. Starts are increasing because timestamps are, so GET_WHEN uses bisect_right(starts, at) - 1 and then checks at < end. Each query costs O(log versions).
pitfalls: ttl = 0 means the value never expires, not that it expires at once.
End is exclusive: a value set at 5 with ttl 5 is gone at time 10.
Deleting an already-expired field must not extend or change its end.
Historical time 0 is a real timestamp. Do not treat it as 'now'.
